item.text:
## 2B.7 Research Note: Narendra Modi in 2024

**Assessment:** Strong support. In 2024, Modi repeatedly used diplomatic channels on the Russia-Ukraine war, backed a lawful peace framework, and kept engagement open after his Kyiv visit. I found **no direct 2024 evidence** that he rejected credible ceasefire or peace-talk opportunities; the only counterweight is continued strategic alignment with Russia.

### Accepted claims

| Title | Publisher | Date | URL | Claim-level summary | IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| [Prime Minister Narendra Modi speaks with President Putin](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleseDetailm.aspx?PRID=2015682) | Prime Minister’s Office / PIB | 20 Mar 2024 | https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleseDetailm.aspx?PRID=2015682 | Modi said India’s consistent position on the Russia-Ukraine conflict was in favor of **dialogue and diplomacy** and that he would stay in touch. This is direct evidence of pursuing peace talks when available. | 2B.7, 2B.1, 1B.1, 1B.8 |
| [India-Ukraine Joint Statement on the Visit of Prime Minister of India to Ukraine](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2048245&lang=2&reg=48) | Prime Minister’s Office / PIB | 23 Aug 2024 | https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2048245&lang=2&reg=48 | The two leaders reiterated readiness to uphold international law and said India had a principled focus on **peaceful resolution through dialogue and diplomacy**. India also participated in the Ukraine peace summit process. This is strong evidence for lawful settlement and peace-talk pursuit. | 2B.7, 2B.1, 1B.1, 1B.8 |
| [Prime Minister’s meeting with the President of Ukraine](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2048240) | Prime Minister’s Office / PIB | 23 Aug 2024 | https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2048240 | Modi’s Kyiv visit produced cooperation agreements and a direct meeting with Zelenskyy, showing active diplomatic engagement rather than military coercion. This supports a reading of **confidence-building and negotiation**. | 2B.7, 2B.1, 1B.8 |
| [Prime Minister Narendra Modi speaks with President Putin](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2049059) | Prime Minister’s Office / PIB | 27 Aug 2024 | https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2049059 | After visiting Ukraine, Modi again stressed the importance of **dialogue, diplomacy, and practical engagement between all stakeholders** for an abiding and peaceful resolution. This is the clearest evidence of continued peace-talk pursuit after a major crisis visit. | 2B.7, 2B.1, 1B.8 |
| [Prime Minister’s meeting with the President of Ukraine](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2058086&lang=1&reg=3) | Prime Minister’s Office / PIB | 24 Sep 2024 | https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2058086&lang=1&reg=3 | Modi reiterated India’s “clear, consistent and constructive approach” in favor of a peaceful resolution through dialogue and dialogue, and said India remained open to support a lasting settlement. This is strong evidence for a lawful, negotiated end-state. | 2B.7, 2B.1, 1B.1, 1B.8 |

### Weak counterweight

| Title | Publisher | Date | URL | Claim-level summary | IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| [Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi speaks with President Putin](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleseDetailm.aspx?PRID=1996327) | Prime Minister’s Office / PIB | 15 Jan 2024 | https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleseDetailm.aspx?PRID=1996327 | Modi also agreed to further strengthen the India-Russia strategic partnership. This does **not** show rejection of peace efforts, but it is the main counterweight because it shows continued alignment with Russia while the war continued. | 2B.7, 1B.1 |

### Search gap

- I found **no direct 2024 evidence** that Modi rejected a credible ceasefire, blocked peace talks, or refused a lawful settlement when one was on offer.
- I also found **no direct evidence** of a Modi-led post-conflict reconciliation program beyond Ukraine-facing humanitarian, trade, and cultural cooperation.
- The record is therefore **consistently peace-oriented**, with the main ambiguity being ongoing strategic cooperation with Russia rather than hostility to settlement efforts.
